title: Resolution-limited cast-shadow silhouette
observations: The moving crater shadow appeared visually strange to the human reviewer.
Constant-material isolation reproduced a stepped cast-shadow boundary.
Disabling cast shadows removed the stepped component but retained smooth directional shading.
Halving native sample spacing from 0.5 m to 0.25 m refined the silhouette while seam and topology checks remained clean.
Cascade range, split mode, split blending, soft-shadow angle, and bias experiments did not remove the resolution-correlated silhouette.
bounded_conclusion: Evidence is consistent with a shadow cast by the polygonal terrain silhouette at the declared sample resolution.
No evidence currently attributes this observation to Transvoxel table, seam, topology, texture projection, or mapped-normal incorrectness.
Human review did not identify a rejectable shadow defect in the declared 0.25 m TQP-25 adversarial fixture.
This does not establish production visual acceptability outside the accepted reference corpus.
closure_scope: TQP-25 Windows reference visual-quality corpus at its declared fixture resolutions

disposition.TQP-23: Retain the finding to distinguish correct shadow attachment from production smoothness within the accepted bounded surface-shading scope.
disposition.TQP-25: Closed for the accepted four-fixture Windows reference corpus by TQP-D015.
disposition.production: Reopen if the silhouette does not scale with geometry resolution, if a world-space boundary slides, pops, or changes topology, or if production review finds the behavior unacceptable.
